page: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB per core, and includes 480 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core profile, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core scores in the top 25%. Single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also perform strongly. However, multi-core and parallelized workloads show limitations; Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with large-block read and write speeds landing in the middle 50%, though cached small-block reads are weaker.

The server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint without the need for high vCPU counts. However, the 2-vCPU limit restricts its suitability for highly parallelized tasks, as evidenced by weak database operations, low Redis SET throughput, and poor static web serving performance. This configuration is best suited for memory-intensive single-threaded applications, lightweight caching layers, or development environments requiring substantial memory but moderate compute power.

It features 16.0 GB of RAM and 480 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance in the top 10% and strong single-threaded compression results. This server provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, offering qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, single-threaded tasks, and development environments.
